# BuildingTea NYC

> Paste any New York City street address and get a plain-English report on the building, built only from the city's own public records: housing violations, heat and hot water complaints, pests and bedbugs, elevators, who the landlord is, and court cases. Free to look up; a one-time purchase unlocks the full report, and an optional monthly "watch" emails you when the city's records for that building change.

BuildingTea is at https://buildingtea.com (buildingteanyc.com redirects there). It covers all five boroughs. There are no user accounts: a purchase is identified by its Stripe checkout session, and the full report is reached through an emailed link. No score or rating is assigned to any building; the report explains the records and says how old they are.

## How it works

- Address lookup uses NYC Planning's GeoSearch to resolve the address to a building (BIN) and tax lot (BBL).
- The report queries NYC Open Data (data.cityofnewyork.us) live for that building: HPD violations and complaints, HPD registration (owner and managing agent), DOB complaints, ECB/OATH violations, elevator records, bedbug filings, vacate orders, housing court cases, 311 requests, and PLUTO building facts.
- Every number in a report is traceable to a named public dataset, listed at the bottom of each report with its last-updated date.
- Reports are generated per search and are not listed publicly; only the home page is in the sitemap.

## Pages

- [Home](https://buildingtea.com/): search box. Type an address and pick the building from the suggestions.
- [Privacy](https://buildingtea.com/privacy) and [Terms](https://buildingtea.com/terms): short plain-English policies. Support: frank@lifeisfake.com.
- Report pages live under /r/ and are created by a search. The free version shows the building facts and record counts; the paid version shows the six questions answered in full.

## Pricing

- Free: look up a building and see the teaser.
- One-time purchase: the full report for one building.
- Monthly watch: once a month, a re-check of the building's city records, a refreshed report, and an email with a short note on what changed; cancel any time.

## Data sources

- NYC Planning GeoSearch: https://geosearch.planninglabs.nyc/docs/
- NYC Open Data: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/
